title: Resort Landing Pages for Packages and Campaigns
excerpt: How to build a landing page for each resort offer, from weekend getaways to offsites and weddings: what to show above the fold, matching ads to pages, and enquiry vs instant booking.
description: Resort landing pages for packages and campaigns: one page per offer, what goes above the fold, matching ads to pages, and enquiry vs instant-book.
html:
A resort landing page is a single page built for one offer, such as a weekend getaway, corporate offsite, wedding or long stay, that a guest reaches from an ad, a social post or a search. It should show the offer, price, inclusions and one clear next step above the fold, and match exactly what the ad promised.

Why one page per offer beats sending everyone to the home page

Your home page has to serve everyone: families, couples, offsite planners, wedding enquiries and returning guests. When someone clicks an ad for "corporate offsite near Bengaluru" and lands on a home page showing a honeymoon couple by the pool, they have to search for what they came for. Many will not.

A dedicated page for each offer does three things. It answers one guest's questions without distraction. It lets you match ad wording and page wording closely, which tends to improve ad quality and cost. And it makes measurement simple: each page has one job, so you can see whether it is doing it.

The four offers most resorts need pages for

Weekend getaway

For guests from nearby cities, such as Bengaluru to Coorg or Mumbai to Lonavala. They want the total price for two nights, what is included, drive time, and whether the weekend they have in mind is available. This page should usually allow instant booking.

Corporate offsite

For HR teams and managers planning a day or overnight event for 15 to 80 people. They need meeting room capacity, AV and Wi-Fi details, sample agendas, meal options, activity options, room count and sharing options, GST invoicing and a contact person. This is almost always an enquiry page.

Wedding or family function

For families planning a destination wedding, engagement or milestone birthday. They want venue capacity for each function, room count for guests, catering and décor options, permissions and timings, and a sense of the budget range. Enquiry page, with a fast human reply.

Long stay or workation

For remote workers and long-stay guests, often in the off season. They want weekly or monthly rates, Wi-Fi speed and power backup, a desk, laundry, meal plans and what is nearby. This can be instant-book for fixed durations, or enquiry for custom dates.

You may also need pages for seasonal offers such as monsoon packages, New Year, or school holidays. Each gets the same structure.

What goes above the fold

"Above the fold" is what a visitor sees on a phone before scrolling. On a resort landing page, it should include:

  • A headline that repeats the offer: "Two-night weekend getaway in Coorg, breakfast and dinner included".
  • One image that shows the offer, not a generic view: the meeting hall for offsites, the lawn set up for a wedding, a family at the pool for a weekend package.
  • Price or price guidance: "From ₹14,500 for two, per night, including taxes" or, for weddings, a clear starting range.
  • Three or four key inclusions as short lines.
  • One primary button: "Check dates" for instant-book pages, "Send enquiry" or "WhatsApp us" for enquiry pages.
  • A trust signal: your Google or OTA rating with a link, or a short real review excerpt.

Below the fold, add the detail: full inclusions, room types, a sample itinerary or agenda, policies, how to get there, FAQs specific to that offer, and the button repeated.

Match the ad to the page

The most common landing page problem is a mismatch between what the ad says and what the page shows. If the ad says "Monsoon offer: third night free", the page headline should say the same and the booking engine should apply it. If the ad mentions a price, the page should show that price.

Ad elementPage must show
Offer nameSame name in the headline
PriceSame price, with what it includes and any conditions
ImageSame or very similar image at the top
Dates or seasonValidity dates clearly stated
Call to actionSame action: book, enquire or WhatsApp
Location claimDrive time or distance stated honestly

For Google Ads, group keywords tightly by offer so each ad group points to its own page. For Meta ads, match the creative closely. Our PPC management page describes how we build these structures, and the post on Google Ads for stays covers the campaign side.

Enquiry pages versus instant-book pages

Not every offer should push guests straight into a booking engine. The choice depends on how standard the offer is.

  • Instant-book suits fixed packages with standard rooms, set inclusions and known prices: weekend getaways, monsoon packages, anniversary stays.
  • Enquiry suits anything that needs a conversation: offsites, weddings, large groups, custom long stays.

For instant-book pages, link the button directly to the booking engine with the package pre-selected, if your engine supports it. Do not make guests find the package again.

For enquiry pages, keep the form short: name, phone, approximate dates, group size, and one free-text box. Offer WhatsApp as an alternative, since many Indian guests prefer it. Then reply quickly; the post on booking engine conversion covers reply speed and follow-up.

A landing page checklist

  • One offer, one page, one main button.
  • Headline matches the ad or post that sends traffic.
  • Total price or clear price guidance, with taxes stated.
  • Inclusions and exclusions listed plainly.
  • Offer validity dates and any blackout dates.
  • Photos specific to the offer.
  • Policies relevant to this guest: child age, cancellation, group deposits.
  • How to get there, with drive time from the main source city.
  • Loads fast on a phone over mobile data.
  • Button click and form submission tracked in GA4.
  • Main site navigation reduced, so guests stay on the offer.

Testing and improving landing pages

Once a page has steady traffic, make one change at a time and watch the result over a few weeks: a different headline, a clearer price, a shorter form, or WhatsApp in place of a form. Small properties rarely have enough traffic for formal A/B testing, so compare periods carefully and note seasonal effects. For deeper work on this, see conversion optimisation.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a separate page for every package?

For any offer you promote with ads, social posts or email, yes. Each needs a page that matches the promotion and answers that guest's questions. Minor variations, such as the same weekend package in two room types, can share one page with options. Start with the two or three offers that bring the most revenue and add pages as you launch new promotions.

Should resort landing pages show prices?

Wherever possible. Guests who cannot see a price often assume it is high and leave. For fixed packages, show the total price including taxes. For weddings and offsites, show a starting price or typical range with what it covers. A clear price also filters out enquiries that are far outside your range, which saves your team time.

Is a WhatsApp button better than an enquiry form?

For many Indian guests, WhatsApp feels faster and more personal, and it is often preferred for weekend and family stays. Corporate planners may still prefer email or a form. Offering both usually works best. Whatever the channel, the reply speed matters most: a quick, helpful response does more than the choice of button.

Can I use the same landing page for Google and Instagram ads?

You can, if the offer and message are the same. In practice, Instagram visitors often arrive with less intent and respond better to more images and a softer call to action, while Google searchers want price and availability quickly. If both audiences are significant, a shared page with a strong top section works; separate pages are worth testing later.

Where to start

List the offers you currently promote and note which page each ad or post links to. Build one dedicated page for your highest-revenue offer using the above-the-fold list here, and point its ads to it. Track button clicks in GA4 for a month before building the next one.
